terms.gloss: the folder of mail received: an inbox
terms.grammar: scrīnium, scrīniī n. with the genitive plural
terms.comment: A description of ours, built on the lexicon’s word for a folder (scrīnium, the case in which papers and letters were kept) and on litterās accipere, to receive a letter. No reference work we searched (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi–Bini) has a word for an inbox. In talk the folder is seldom named; one says what has come (see the examples).

phrases.english: Let’s see what email has come.

phrases.latin: iīs tantum rescrīpsī ā quibus accēperam
phrases.english: I have written back only to those from whom I had received letters

sources: Lewis & Short: scrinium · Lewis & Short: littera · Lewis & Short: accipio
